text:
alex: Heads up — I've been digging into traces from the inference fleet and we're getting wildly different span attribute shapes across Python/Go/Rust. Dashboards are noisy and latency percentiles don't line up.

maria_l: ugh that explains the weird charts I saw this morning. which attrs in particular?

alex: mostly `model.name`, `model.version`, `route` vs `endpoint`, and sometimes `batch.size` is missing from Go spans. Python has `http.status_code` while Rust emits `http.status`.

jia_wu: are we conflating semantic conventions across SDKs? OTEL has spec but everyone interprets it a bit.

owen: can you paste an example span?

alex: sure — from python service:
```
Span(name="inference.request")
attributes={"model.name":"gpt-4o", "model.version":"2026-02-12", "http.status_code":200, "batch.size":4}
```
and from rust:
```
Span(name="inference")
attributes={"model":"gpt-4o","version":"2026-02-12","http.status":200}
```

samir: classic. dashboards and alert rules assume `model.name`. Our retention labels in trace storage use `model.name` so Rust traces drop out of some rollups.

maria_l: this is problematic for query cost too — inconsistent keys mean more cardinality when we try to aggregate.

telemetry-bot: automated-check: found 37k spans in last 24h missing attribute `model.name` across services tagged "inference"

alex: proposal: create a tiny internal OTEL shim (libredwood-otel?) that normalizes attribute names and enforces a minimal set of resource attributes at span creation time. It would be a tiny wrapper in each language with the same env var-driven config.

jia_wu: I'm +1. How would we handle semantic conventions vs our custom keys? e.g. `http.status` vs `http.status_code` — prefer spec but we need a compatibility mapping.

owen: mapping table sounds right. keep existing spec keys as canonical (http.status_code) and translate variants to the canonical form when present. also add `redwood.model.name` if they want proprietary tag?

samir: we should avoid duplicating attributes — do mapping then drop the old key. Also normalize types (string vs int). Lots of services currently set version as int in go, string in python.

maria_l: what about performance? wrapper can't add blocking work or sync network calls. Needs to be local attribute mapping only.

alex: agreed — purely in-process, no network. small impact on allocation; can be optimized in Rust/Go. For python we can do lazy normalization on span end.

jia_wu: shutdown/exporter semantics: if we depend on SDK shutdown to flush attributes, that complicates serverless / quick process patterns. We should ensure normalization happens at span start and end deterministically.

nowen: also consider batching/exporter buffering differences. Go exporter drops unknown resource attributes by default in our current setup; the shim should ensure resource attr `service.instance.id` is always set so storage grouping works.

samir: here's a prototype config idea: 
```
# envs for shim
REDWOOD_OTEL_SHIM=1
REDWOOD_OTEL_NORMALIZE_MAP=model:model.name,version:model.version,http.status:http.status_code
REDWOOD_OTEL_ENFORCED_RES=service.name:inference,service.platform:edge
```

maria_l: nice. How do we rollout? Want to avoid flipping on everywhere and spamming traces.

alex: propose staged rollout: add shim to all services but disabled by default. Canary the normalization on a small set of hosts using config flag (we have feature flags tied to clusters). Step 1: enable shim but `DRY_RUN=1` which logs a single metric for mismatches. Step 2: enable for 5% of traffic, monitor dashboards and OTLP ingest costs. Step 3: global enable.

jia_wu: DRY_RUN is nice. we can emit a counter metric `redwood.otel.normalization.mismatch` with labels for service/lang to measure impact.

telemetry-bot: metric emitted: redwood.otel.normalization.mismatch count=0 since last deploy

owen: for Rust crate, we can add a feature flag `shim_normalize` and also expose a `normalize_span(attrs: &mut Attributes)` fn so services can call it explicitly in hot paths (avoid wrapper overhead).

samir: for Go, a middleware that hooks into context before span start makes sense. For Python we should provide both decorator and auto-instrumentation patch that runs normalization. But watch out for duplicating with opentelemetry-instrumentation libs.

maria_l: testing: we need an integration test that sends spans from each lang and asserts normalized keys in the collector. We can stand up an otlp collector in CI and run quick e2e.

alex: agreed. Also add a changelog and docs page in the ops-runbook explaining canonical keys and the mapping table.

jia_wu: one more: sampling interaction. We must ensure normalization occurs before sampler decision if we're going to sample based on attributes like `model.name`. Otherwise sampled traces are inconsistent.

samir: good catch — normalize early (on span start) and then let sampler run. Some SDKs allow custom samplers that inspect attributes on creation. We'll document that requirement.

nowen: security/privacy note — make sure normalization doesn't create new PII attributes we weren't collecting. mapping only, no new extraction.

alex: ok next steps: 1) I'll open a tiny RFC with mapping table + env options. 2) jia + owen + samir to sketch language wrappers. 3) maria to update dashboards and add mismatch counters to alerts. 4) small canary rollout next week.

maria_l: happy to own dashboard changes. adding a new alert for mismatch rate > 0.1% sounds reasonable.

jia_wu: I'll prototype python shim today, ping if you want pair.

owen: I'll do go middleware and the rust normalize fn.

samir: I'll hook the CI e2e and toy collector.

telemetry-bot: noted: RFC issue created (#3142) by alex. Canaries planned: 5% -> 20% -> 100%

alex: thanks all. if anyone sees odd spikes in tokenization/span counts after canary, ping #incidents. :thumbsup:

maria_l: :thumbsup:
